These form a stochastic process over player-state manifolds, where each primitive defines a failure mode or transition condition. The blocking error primitive acts as a hard gate, enforcing build-time correctness. The stale assignment primitive models temporal inconsistency through a time-based threshold. The conflicting assignment primitive introduces a logical disjunction between canonical and fallback states, requiring explicit conflict records. These operators are dual to each other in that they both represent breakdowns in data fidelity but differ in their resolution paths—either by enforcement or by triggering manual intervention. The system's robustness depends on these primitives' ability to detect and isolate inconsistencies before propagation into downstream systems.
